title: Forgiving Others
definition: Forgiving Others is the Christlike release of bitterness and personal vengeance because God has forgiven us in Christ.
summary: Forgiving Others is the believer's grace-shaped release of personal vengeance because God has forgiven in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ purchased forgiveness for sinners and calls His people to extend mercy to others.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Forgiving others is the believer's grace-shaped release of personal vengeance because God has forgiven them in Christ. Scripture commands forgiveness while still taking sin seriously.

Forgiveness does not mean pretending evil did not happen, removing all consequences, or ignoring wisdom and safety. It means entrusting justice to God and refusing to live chained to revenge.

Jesus forgave His enemies and purchased forgiveness for His people. Believers forgive from the mercy they have received, not from denial of pain.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Bitterness can quietly shape a person's heart long after the wound occurred. Forgiving others protects the soul from vengeance while honoring the seriousness of grace.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring the offense honestly before God. Ask Him to help you release revenge, pursue reconciliation where wise and possible, and maintain boundaries where safety or repentance requires them.
